description: Validated scientific literature relevant to algorithms and scientific data products implemented or maintained in Spyctres. Links are checked before entries are added; affected_code identifies where each reference informs behavior.

references.citation: Cappellari, M. (2017), Improving the full spectrum fitting method: accurate convolution with Gauss-Hermite functions, Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society, 466, 798-811.
references.validated_via: Crossref metadata and DOI resolution
references.description: Develops an analytic Fourier-domain treatment of line-of-sight and instrumental broadening that remains accurate near the Nyquist sampling limit. Spyctres uses this rationale for its Gaussian log-wavelength FFT convolution, including an analytic kernel transform rather than a directly sampled narrow kernel.

references.citation: Husser, T.-O. et al. (2013), A new extensive library of PHOENIX stellar atmospheres and synthetic spectra, Astronomy & Astrophysics, 553, A6.
references.validated_via: Publisher article and Crossref metadata
references.description: Describes the PHOENIX synthetic spectral library used by the template backend, including its 2300-12000 K parameter coverage, LTE assumptions, and wavelength conventions. It is the primary scientific reference for the model spectra loaded, interpolated, and fitted by the PHOENIX workflow, and supports the hard guard against using this grid above 12000 K.

references.citation: Ciddor, P. E. (1996), Refractive index of air: new equations for the visible and near infrared, Applied Optics, 35, 1566-1573.
references.validated_via: Optica DOI resolution and Crossref metadata
references.description: Provides the refractive-index relation currently used by Spyctres for explicit air-to-vacuum and vacuum-to-air wavelength conversion. Centralizing this citation makes the adopted wavelength-medium convention auditable and distinguishes it from alternative Edlen or Morton formulations.

references.citation: Carnall, A. C. (2017), SpectRes: A Fast Spectral Resampling Tool in Python, arXiv:1705.05165.
references.validated_via: arXiv abstract and metadata API
references.description: Presents a flux-conserving method for resampling spectral flux densities and uncertainties on arbitrary wavelength grids. The legacy Spyctres binning routine cites this work; its conservation principle also informs validation of modern resampling paths, although the production LSF implementation uses its own tested log-grid rebinning algorithm.

references.citation: Morton, D. C. (2000), Atomic Data for Resonance Absorption Lines. II. Wavelengths Longward of the Lyman Limit for Heavy Elements, The Astrophysical Journal Supplement Series, 130, 403-436.
references.validated_via: IOP DOI resolution and Crossref metadata
references.description: Documents the vacuum-to-air refractive-index convention adopted by VALD3 for wavelengths above 2000 Angstrom. Spyctres exposes this convention as the vacuum-to-air half of the explicitly selected vald3 conversion method rather than silently mixing it with the Ciddor implementation.

references.citation: Birch, K. P. & Downs, M. J. (1994), Correction to the Updated Edlen Equation for the Refractive Index of Air, Metrologia, 31, 315-316.
references.validated_via: IOP DOI resolution and Crossref metadata
references.description: Provides the corrected refractive-index basis cited by Morton and the VALD3 wavelength-conversion documentation. It establishes the physical dry-air conditions underlying the vald3 conversion, which are distinct from the separately available Ciddor method.

references.citation: VALD3 Documentation, Wavelength conversion air <-> vacuum, including the reversible air-to-vacuum inverse derived by N. Piskunov.
references.validated_via: Official VALD documentation page and coefficient comparison
references.description: This is the authoritative technical source for the exact Piskunov inverse coefficients historically embedded in the legacy get_element_lines implementation. The formula is paired with the Morton vacuum-to-air relation, is defined only above 2000 Angstrom, and is retained as an explicitly named compatibility method.

references.citation: NASA Exoplanet Archive, PEPSI Exoplanet Transit Survey (PETS) Data at the Exoplanet Archive.
references.validated_via: Official NASA Exoplanet Archive page; product description and FITS-column documentation inspected
references.description: Documents PETS Arg as air wavelength in microns and states that the wavelength array has already been shifted to the stellar centre-of-mass rest frame using RADVEL and OBSVEL. This is the authority for the opt-in PETS reader profile and its guard against applying an observer correction a second time.

references.citation: Ilyin, I. (2020), PEPSI Spectroscopic Data Systems: Data Reduction User Manual, Version 1.0.
references.validated_via: Official PEPSI PDF; pipeline, wavelength-calibration, slice-merging, and DXT naming sections inspected
references.description: Describes PEPSI SDS reduction stages and identifies DXT as a slicer/side designation. It supports the rule that a .dxt.nor filename is not evidence for a wavelength reference frame, so release-specific semantics must be selected from documentation or headers.

references.citation: CDS ReadMe for A&A 671, A7 (2023), PEPSI spectra data-product description.
references.validated_via: Official CDS ReadMe; Arg column unit and Solar-System-barycentric scale inspected
references.description: Documents a PEPSI release whose Arg column is in Angstrom and on the Solar System barycentric wavelength scale. It demonstrates why PEPSI release profiles must remain explicit and why PETS microns/stellar-rest semantics cannot be inferred for arbitrary .nor files.

references.citation: Verro, K. et al. (2022), The X-shooter Spectral Library (XSL): Data Release 3, Astronomy & Astrophysics, 660, A34.
references.validated_via: Publisher metadata, official XSL DR3 site, and CDS catalogue description
references.description: Defines the XSL DR3 combined-arm, air-wavelength, stellar-rest-frame spectral products and their effective arm-dependent velocity resolutions. It also supplies the Figure 1 reference-star sequence and the adopted parameters for the added M dwarfs. Spyctres uses these semantics for ingestion and empirical PHOENIX classification validation.

references.citation: X-shooter Spectral Library, XSL DR3 Data Format documentation.
references.validated_via: Official XSL project data-format page
references.description: Documents the DR3 FITS table columns, wavelength unit in nm, logarithmic sampling, stellar-rest-frame status, corrected-flux variants, and Gaussian velocity sigma for each effective arm/overlap region. The companion DR3 paper establishes that the wavelengths are in air.

references.citation: Arentsen, A. et al. (2019), Stellar atmospheric parameters for 754 spectra from the X-shooter Spectral Library, Astronomy & Astrophysics, 627, A138.
references.validated_via: A&A publisher article and CDS catalogue J/A+A/627/A138
references.description: Provides homogeneous effective temperatures, surface gravities, metallicities, and uncertainties derived from XSL UVB/VIS spectra. These adopted values form the primary comparison set for seven of the Figure 1 stars; the paper's precision estimates and carbon-star flag prevent the benchmark from treating every reference value as equally secure.

references.citation: Gonneau, A. et al. (2017), Carbon stars in the X-Shooter Spectral Library: II. Comparison with models, Astronomy & Astrophysics, 601, A141.
references.validated_via: A&A publication metadata, arXiv 1702.00819, and the published model-comparison tables
references.description: Derives separate optical and near-infrared atmospheric-parameter ranges for XSL carbon stars using carbon-rich models with C/O as an explicit dimension. For X0013 it favors temperatures near 3400 K, log(g) near 0, and [Fe/H] near -0.5. Because the present Spyctres PHOENIX grid does not fit C/O, X0013 is retained as a deliberate model-mismatch stress test rather than an ordinary accuracy benchmark.

references.citation: Lançon, A. et al. (2021), A comparison between X-shooter spectra and PHOENIX models across the HR-diagram, Astronomy & Astrophysics, 649, A97.
references.validated_via: A&A publisher PDF, DOI metadata, and official XSL papers index
references.description: Directly compares XSL spectra with PHOENIX-based Göttingen models. It finds wavelength-arm-dependent parameter offsets and increasingly structured residuals below about 5000 K, especially in the UVB, providing the scientific basis for reporting individual-star residuals and model-stress categories instead of reducing this validation to a single pass/fail statistic.

references.citation: Kunder, A. et al. (2017), The Radial Velocity Experiment (RAVE): Fifth Data Release, The Astronomical Journal, 153, 75.
references.validated_via: Journal DOI metadata and publisher-version PDF
references.description: Supplies the external RAVE atmospheric parameters used by the XSL DR3 study when assessing LTT 2544. The validation manifest uses the XSL DR3 adopted fit for this star, while this reference records the independent provenance against which that M-dwarf estimate was checked.

references.citation: Cappellari, M. (2023), Full spectrum fitting with photometry in pPXF: stellar population versus dynamical masses, non-parametric star formation history and metallicity for 3200 LEGA-C galaxies at redshift z approximately 0.8, Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society, 526, 3273-3300.
references.validated_via: MNRAS publisher paper, arXiv 2208.14974, and CapFit documentation
references.description: Describes pPXF's separable optimization architecture and CapFit nonlinear least-squares method. It supports Spyctres' decision to solve multiplicative continuum coefficients exactly as a linear subproblem inside each nonlinear atmospheric-parameter evaluation while retaining SciPy's bounded least-squares optimizer for the small nonlinear parameter set.

references.citation: Hobbs, L. M. et al. (2008), A Catalog of Diffuse Interstellar Bands in the Spectrum of HD 204827, The Astrophysical Journal, 680, 1256-1270.
references.validated_via: arXiv abstract and metadata; optical diffuse-interstellar-band catalogue scope inspected
references.description: Presents a high-resolution optical catalogue of diffuse interstellar bands between 3900 and 8100 Angstrom. Spyctres uses this as a general literature basis for treating DIBs as non-photospheric absorption that should be annotated or optionally masked rather than interpreted as missing PHOENIX stellar-atmosphere opacity.

references.citation: García-Hernández, D. A. & Díaz-Luis, J. J. (2013), Diffuse interstellar bands in fullerene planetary nebulae: the fullerenes - diffuse interstellar bands connection, Astronomy & Astrophysics, 550, L6.
references.validated_via: arXiv abstract, DOI metadata, and paper summary mentioning the very broad 4428 Angstrom DIB
references.description: Discusses the very broad 4428 Angstrom diffuse interstellar band and its unusually intense appearance in fullerene-bearing planetary nebulae. Spyctres uses this reference for the explicit DIB 4428 non-stellar feature annotation and optional masking guardrail.

references.citation: Galazutdinov, G. et al. (2020), Survey of very broad Diffuse Interstellar Bands, Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society, 494, 3091-3097.
references.validated_via: arXiv abstract and metadata; paper summary explicitly identifies the very broad 4882 Angstrom DIB
references.description: Studies very broad diffuse interstellar bands, including features at approximately 4430 and 4882 Angstrom. Spyctres uses this reference for the DIB 4882 catalog entry and for warning that absorption near the H-beta red wing may be non-stellar contamination rather than missing PHOENIX stellar opacity.

references.citation: Garcia Perez, A. E. et al. (2016), ASPCAP: The APOGEE Stellar Parameter and Chemical Abundances Pipeline, The Astronomical Journal, 151, 144.
references.validated_via: Published Astronomical Journal paper and SDSS ASPCAP documentation
references.description: Documents ASPCAP/FERRE's use of 12 dispersed initial searches across stellar-parameter space and selection of the lowest-chi-square solution. Spyctres adopts the underlying lesson with a compact sparse-node coarse scan followed by a shared-cache local multistart, rather than copying the survey-specific number or parameter layout.
